note: the same projected margins, converted by two link functions across a σ grid, scored against 60 official finals
reading: the calibration claim that a hard-coded σ=11 makes the model overconfident is NOT supported: on this window the best Brier in the table is logistic_sigma_8 (0.1975), and the error-dispersion σ (17.392) scores worse. The reason is that mean absolute error is dragged up by a handful of blowouts while the typical game is much tighter, so a σ taken from error dispersion overstates uncertainty for the median game. The real defect in scripts/build_edge_site.py is that the constant and the link are typed rather than fitted, not that the value is wrong — and the bias that does survive is the home-court term: mean P(home) sits above the actual home win rate in 2 of 18 variants.
caveat: choosing the best σ from this table IS in-sample selection on 60 games; it is printed to correct an assertion, not to set a parameter
